corrections.source_says: Set to met and revise the corresponding explanation in eligibility.reason. The researchers counted distinct new design ideas in participants' proposals, using proposal coding and think-aloud/walkthrough evidence. Under creativity-codebook.md, Section 6, this is fluency measured by category_count, both already correctly recorded for S1-O1. A separate creativity or novelty rating is not necessary for this fluency outcome. This is a randomized people study for two-screener review, while core remains no because the main study has fewer than 50 people.
corrections.quote: We define idea addition as participants adding ideas in the second iteration that are different from the ideas in their first iteration.
corrections.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 4.1.1; PDF p. 4, Sections 3.3.2-3.3.3; PDF p. 5, Section 3.4.1; creativity-codebook.md, Sections 3 and 6

The other two final-count SDs are not printed and should be null. Add total ideas changed (other): Interactive Engagement M = 3.47, SD = 1.51; omnibus H(2) = 1.20, p = .548. Add ideas deleted (other): three Interactive Engagement participants deleted four ideas, two Stepwise Guidance participants deleted three ideas, and Self Reflection had no deletions; these idea totals are not participant sample sizes. Expand the existing edit measure_detail to retain the reported components: enhancements, Guidance versus Reflection p_adj = .036 and Engagement versus Reflection p_adj = .030; revisions, Engagement versus Reflection p_adj = .023. Five Engagement participants revised six ideas, one Guidance participant revised one idea, and Reflection participants revised none. No additional standardized effects or unprinted SDs should be calculated.

confirmed: Read the entire markdown conversion and all 15 PDF pages, including Appendices A-G. The title, authors Howard Ziyu Han and Nikolas Martelaro, and source.version are supported by the local PDF: arXiv:2608.04166v1 [cs.HC], 4 Aug 2026 (PDF p. 1; appendices pp. 11-15).

The main study randomly assigned 45 individual design students to Self Reflection, Stepwise Guidance, or Interactive Engagement while redesigning a civic reporting website; the supervised Zoom session supports lab_rct, and context_class = none is appropriate (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.3-3.3.2).

The main study reports 45 recruited and randomized people, 45 collected design proposals, and 90 iterations, with all proposals coded; no exclusions are reported. This supports the form's 45-person analysis count and core = no under the 50-person threshold; 90 is an iteration count, not a people count (PDF p. 4, Section 3.3.2; p. 5, Sections 3.4-3.4.1).
The Interactive Engagement denominator of 15 is explicit in the statement that 14 of 15 participants used the steering frames (PDF p. 7, Section 4.3.1).

Mean age 25.08 (SD 3.68), mean design/HCI study experience 4 years (SD 1.79), approximately 90 minutes overall, first iteration 20-30 minutes, condition phase 15 minutes, and second iteration 15-25 minutes all match the PDF (p. 4, Section 3.3.2).

The AI arm uses GPT-4.1 for critique, GPT-4o for visual parsing, and Whisper for voice input; it receives two rounds of four stakeholder pushback points, delivered through researcher-operated fixed triggers (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1-3.3.2; pp. 12-13, Appendix D).
The Self Reflection instructions specify about 12 minutes without edits followed by about 3 minutes sharing thoughts (PDF p. 13, Appendix E).

All values in S1-O1.reported match Section 4.1.1: H(2) = 9.12, p = .010, epsilon^2 = .21; Reflection M = 2.13, SD = 1.36; Guidance M = 0.80, SD = 1.15, versus Reflection p_adj = .008, g = -1.03; Engagement M = 1.27, SD = 0.80, versus Reflection p_adj = .446 and versus Guidance p_adj = .346 (PDF p. 5).

All values in S1-O2.reported match Section 4.1.2: H(2) = 12.42, p = .002, epsilon^2 = .28; Engagement M = 1.93, SD = 0.96, versus Reflection p_adj = .002, g = 1.45; Guidance M = 1.60, SD = 1.24, versus Reflection p_adj = .031, g = 0.95; Reflection M = 0.53, SD = 0.92; Guidance versus Engagement is not significant (PDF pp. 5-6).

All values in S1-O3.reported match Section 4.2.4: H(2) = 8.30, p = .016, epsilon^2 = .19; Engagement M = 5.47, SD = 1.252, versus Reflection p_adj = .030, g = 0.93; Guidance M = 5.47, SD = 1.246, versus Reflection p_adj = .048, g = 0.93; Reflection M = 4.00, SD = 1.77 (PDF p. 7).

The reconsideration item wording used in the form is verbatim from Appendix F; this is a self-report on a 7-point scale, correctly marked scored_on_output = false (PDF p. 14, Critical Design Thinking; p. 4, Section 3.3.3).

The one-line finding accurately reproduces the textual results: more edits with Engagement than Reflection (1.93 versus 0.53, p_adj = .002, g = 1.45), no significant difference in additions (1.27 versus 2.13, p_adj = .446), and no creativity rating of the proposals (PDF pp. 4-6, Sections 3.3.3-4.1.2; p. 14, Appendix F).

Source inconsistency: Figure 2 labels the mean addition segments 2.4 for Reflection and 0.9 for Guidance, whereas Section 4.1.1 prints 2.13 and 0.80. The existing reported strings correctly reproduce the results text; the conflicting figure labels should be flagged, not substituted for those text values (PDF p. 5, Figure 2 and Section 4.1.1).

The six formative expert interviewees and three preliminary pilot tests are separate from the main randomized sample. The pilots rate AI critique points, and neither preliminary component supplies another randomized comparison of creativity on human output (PDF p. 2, Section 3.1; pp. 3-4, Section 3.2; p. 12, Appendix B).

The paper refers to a supplementary coding codebook without a link; the local PDF includes Appendices A-G but not that full codebook. The codebase is promised upon acceptance, and this PDF provides no public data/code URL (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2 and 3.3.3; pp. 11-15).
This is an original experiment rather than a synthesis, so the empty synthesis fields are appropriate; it reports no pooled study estimate (PDF pp. 2-8, Sections 3-7).

The revision phase follows the feedback phase, but the paper does not explicitly state that AI-generated sticky notes were removed. Phase order alone does not establish an unassisted after_ai outcome (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.1 and 3.3.2; pp. 12-13, Appendix D).
summary: The paper contains a randomized study of 45 design students with output-coded idea fluency and should receive two-screener review, although it remains below the core sample-size cutoff. The existing reported statistics and source version are accurate, but output eligibility, the written-guidance group count and its description, and the inventory of output measures need correction.
